query: I'm extending my conference paper into a journal article. The journal follows Springer's rule for extended proceedings papers. Here are both versions. Is it extended enough, and can you draft the summary of differences?
expected_behavior: Runs scripts/compare_versions.py on the two files with --threshold 30
Reports an overall new-text estimate of about 47 percent (between 40 and 55) and says it meets 30 percent as a text estimate only, not as proof of compliance
Identifies 'Adaptive threshold' and 'Field evaluation' as entirely new sections, and 'Method' and 'Evaluation' as carried over unchanged
Flags that about three quarters of the abstract is carried over word for word and recommends rewriting it
Flags that the draft has no sentence disclosing the conference paper, although the paper appears in the references, and drafts a disclosure for the introduction
Drafts a summary of differences that lists the adaptive threshold with its false alarm bound and the six-week field deployment, using only numbers that appear in the draft
Mentions Springer's requirement for an explicit statement about the increment, or recommends checking the journal's own policy

query: My 6-page ACM conference paper on a cache replacement policy got invited to a special issue of extended best papers. I haven't started the journal version. What should I add, and what will the editors expect?
expected_behavior: Asks for or looks up the special issue call and the journal's policy, noting that a special issue call often sets its own rules
Mentions ACM's general guideline of at least 25 percent new material and says editors judge new contributions, not added length
Asks for the paper's limitations, future work, or reviews to find extension candidates instead of inventing results
Lists the required changes: a new or different title, a rewritten abstract, a citation and disclosure of the conference paper, and updated related work
Notes that ACM lets authors reuse their own text in a new work with a citation and the DOI of the version of record
Does not write a summary of differences with invented content

query: We're extending our 8-page IEEE conference paper for IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications. My coauthor says IEEE requires exactly 30% new content. Is that right, and what do we need to submit?
expected_behavior: Explains that IEEE has no single IEEE-wide percentage and that ComSoc journals require substantial differences judged by the editor, describing the 30 percent figure as an old rule

Lists the ComSoc items: cite the conference version in the submission system and in the paper, use an at least slightly different title, and upload a summary of differences because the conference paper is 8 pages or longer
Recommends confirming the current policy on the journal's own page
Does not present any numeric threshold as official IEEE policy
